# Naim Bin Hasan

> Naim Bin Hasan is a PhD researcher in Information Science and Technology at the Syracuse University School of Information Studies (iSchool), Syracuse, New York. He studies AI and the future of work, human-computer interaction, digital labor and online freelancers, and ICT for development (ICT4D). Before research, he worked as a full-stack web developer with 100+ freelance projects on Fiverr and Upwork. He is cited as Hasan, N. B.

## Current position
- PhD, Information Science and Technology, Syracuse University iSchool (Fall 2026 to present), fully funded through a Graduate Research Assistantship.
- Graduate Research Assistant on Gravity Spy, the citizen-science project supporting the LIGO gravitational-wave observatory: interactive web tools, AI-supported learning resources and trace-data analysis.
- Research practicum (IST 810) with the AI Programming Research Group and Dr. Kevin Crowston: analysis of about 7,000 student interactions with the AI tutor chatbot in IST 256, Syracuse's introductory Python course.

## Education
- MA, Sociology, Florida Atlantic University (2024 to 2026). Thesis: "Trading Precarities: How Bangladeshi Freelancers Leverage the Digital Economy Amid Local Insecurity and AI Disruption" (24 in-depth interviews).
- MSS and BSS (Honours), Sociology, University of Dhaka (2017 to 2024).
- Professional Certificate, Full Stack Software Development, IBM via Coursera (May 2024).

## Publications
- Hasan, N. B. (2025). AI efficiency vs human empathy: A paradox of AI and human agents in service support interactions. Sociology Lens (Wiley). https://doi.org/10.1111/johs.70027
- Hasan, N. B. (2026). Trading precarities: How Bangladeshi freelancers leverage the digital economy amid local insecurity and AI disruption [Master's thesis, Florida Atlantic University]. https://digitalcommons.fau.edu/etd_general/311
- Survival or Transition? How AI Reconfigures Work, Control, and Inequality in the Global South (revise and resubmit).
- The Growth of Online Freelancing in Bangladesh: Economic Integration and Labor Vulnerability (talk, 14th Annual SAGGSA Conference, Florida International University, 2025).
- Conferences: 4th Annual Intellectual Resistance Conference (FAU, 2026; paper presenter and one of four organizers); Mid-South Sociological Association 51st Annual Conference (2025); 14th Annual SAGGSA Conference (FIU, 2025).
